summary: This program builds a playlist of Song objects, then stores the same songs in two kinds of maps keyed by title: a HashMap, whose iteration order is unpredictable, and a TreeMap, which keeps its keys sorted alphabetically. Printing both side by side shows the difference between the two implementations of the Map interface.

lines.text: Map is the interface that both HashMap and TreeMap implement, so declaring variables of this type lets you swap implementations without changing the rest of the code.
The playlist starts as an ordered list, which keeps songs in the order you added them.
Each Song carries a title, artist, genre, and energy level; the titles here are deliberately not in alphabetical order so the TreeMap's sorting is visible later.
An enhanced for loop walks the list once, handing you each Song in turn.
A map stores key-value pairs; here the key is a song title (a String) and the value is the whole Song object, so you can look a song up by name.
put inserts a pair into the map, using the song's title as its key.
keySet returns every key in the map; a HashMap gives no guarantee about the order they come out in, which is the point of the comparison.
get looks up the value stored under a key, which is the fast retrieval that makes maps worth using.
Passing an existing map to the TreeMap constructor copies all of its pairs in, and the TreeMap immediately reorders them by key.
Iterating a TreeMap always visits keys in sorted order, so the titles print alphabetically without any explicit sorting step.
